audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows disagree with their own why text: row 0 reads Neeko while whys[0] says you have no combo yet, row 2 reads Zac while whys[2] calls it a trade his sustain can't answer, row 3 reads Zac while whys[3] says 'even', and row 5 reads Zac while whys[5] says your first item shreds him.
audit.why: Packet chart is [Skill, Skill, Neeko, Skill, Neeko, Neeko, Zac] and matches the prose on all seven rows. Win rate 50% over 8 games — too thin to lean on, so the prose and the packet carry the decision.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3 and 5 to the packet values as one atomic pair-matched group; rows 1, 4 and 6 already agree.

audit.why: Four spikes: Lvl 3 Q+E, Lvl 6 Pop Blossom, 1st item Liandry's/Blackfire, Late his tank scaling. The Level 3 window is real — Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1, so a Zac who has spent it cannot answer a root for a full rotation of your 12s E.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's core Level 6 plan is to channel Pop Blossom while disguised so 'he never sees the slam coming'. Against Zac specifically that plan does not work, and the pages state the opposite in three places (whys[4], mid, wants.you[1]).
audit.why: Restating the mirror audit from this side: Neeko's passive breaks on receiving immobilizing crowd control, and both Stretching Strikes (Q) and Elastic Slingshot (E) knock up. So Zac strips the disguise on reaction and exposes the hidden R preparation. The correct order is root first with Tangle-Barbs, then channel — not walk in disguised and hope.
audit.corrected: Root first, then channel; the disguise is not cover against a knockup kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls a spent Elastic Slingshot a 'fifteen-second invitation'; it is 21/18/15/12/9s.
audit.why: 21s at rank 1 is more than double the max-rank figure and is the actual green light the page keeps referring to.
audit.corrected: Replaced with 21s at rank 1, and the same number used in the mid text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer describes him healing off blobs three times and never names Grievous Wounds, and nothing mentions that his passive revives him.
audit.why: Cell Division sheds reabsorbable chunks on every ability hit and, on fatal damage, splits him into 4 bloblets that recombine into a revive. His W also deals percent max health, so building HP against him is a trap. Anti-heal timing and the revive are what decide whether your one 120/105/90s Pop Blossom actually converts.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal folded into whys[1] and the revive stated in spikes[3].

edits.before: Zac burns Elastic Slingshot on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Zac burns Elastic Slingshot on nothing — that is a 21s invitation at rank 1.

edits.before: A second Q point gives you poke, but he heals it back off passive blobs — neither of you commits, so it stays even.
edits.after: A second Q point gives you poke, but Cell Division blobs heal it back — anti-heal early or the chip never sticks.

edits.before: Pop Blossom on a landed E bursts him hard, and ulting while disguised means he can't dodge the channel.
edits.after: Pop Blossom on a landed E bursts him hard, but any Zac knockup strips the disguise — root first, then channel.

edits.before: Zac's biggest threat: a max-HP E sling from fog flips a fight — if his blobs are up he survives your full combo and CCs your carries.
edits.after: Zac's biggest threat: a fog sling flips a fight, and Cell Division revives him off four bloblets, so your full combo has to kill him twice.

edits.before: Hit Level 6 and combo E into Pop Blossom while disguised so he can't pre-dodge
edits.after: Hit Level 6 and root him first — his knockups strip the disguise off your R prep

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are even-ish — you out-poke him but he just eats it and sustains off blobs, so don't overstay or he slings (E) onto you when your W and shields are down. Level 6 is your window: a landed E into Pop Blossom bursts a real chunk off him, and because you can channel the ult while disguised as a minion or clone, he never sees the slam coming. Bait his E sling first — once it's on cooldown he has no engage and no escape, and that's when you all-in.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are even-ish — you out-poke him but he just eats it and sustains off blobs, so don't overstay or Elastic Slingshot lands on you when your W and shields are down. Level 6 is your window: a landed E into Pop Blossom bursts a real chunk off him, but his Q and E both knock up and any knockup strips your disguise mid-prep, so root him first and channel after. Bait the sling — down 21s at rank 1, he has no engage and no escape.

notes: Mirror reuse: the zac__neeko audit's key finding was that Inherent Glamour breaks on immobilizing crowd control and both of Zac's knockups (Stretching Strikes, Elastic Slingshot) strip it on reaction. This page was telling the player the exact opposite — that disguise makes the Pop Blossom channel unseeable — in whys[4], mid and wants.you[1]. All three now say root first, channel second, which states the same fact from Neeko's side rather than contradicting the mirror. Chart rows 0, 2, 3 and 5 proposed as one atomic pair-matched group and now match the packet exactly. Two related strings still carry the old disguise plan and did not fit a clean band rewrite: spikes[1].text ('ult disguised as a minion so he never sees the channel coming') and dontsFull ordering — worth a second pass. Sample is only 8 games at 50%, so the chart follows the prose and the packet rather than the win rate.
